eligibility_reason: The paper collects new survey data (N=256 mobile-banking users) to replicate Bhattacherjee's (2001) IS Continuance Model, re-testing all five of its hypothesized paths, and reports that all five are supported.

effects.original_title: Understanding information systems continuance: an expectation-confirmation model
effects.replication_study: single study (cross-sectional survey of mobile banking app users, SEM)
effects.contrast: not applicable: SEM path coefficient, satisfaction -> continuance intention
effects.description: Users' satisfaction with prior IS use is positively associated with their intention to continue using the IS (online banking).
effects.citation_sentence: The focus of this paper is on replicating IS Continuance Model (Bhattacherjee, 2001) in the mobile banking context.
effects.evidence: Section 4.2 / Figure 2 (path 0.432): "The analysis shows that all hypotheses are supported at p < 0.01 level. Continuance intention was predicted by satisfaction and perceived usefulness." Table 3: "Hypotheses Supported: All five hypotheses supported."
effects.notes: Original DOI not given in the paper (references.json has none), so original_url is left blank. The paper gives the author only as 'Bhattacherjee, A.'; the full first name is not stated, so it is not supplied. Replication type: the authors explicitly classify the study as a conceptual replication (Dennis & Valacich 2014 taxonomy: 'This research fits into the conceptual category'), and the codebook tiebreaker gives precedence to the authors' label. By the codebook's own definitions it reads more like a close extension: same theory, same cross-sectional survey and SEM paradigm, items adapted to mobile banking, and a new context and population (mobile apps, 2015, students from several banks). The five hypotheses are coded as separate claims because the original reported each path as a distinct hypothesized finding.

effects.original_title: Understanding information systems continuance: an expectation-confirmation model
effects.replication_study: single study (cross-sectional survey of mobile banking app users, SEM)
effects.contrast: not applicable: SEM path coefficient, confirmation -> satisfaction
effects.description: Users' extent of confirmation of expectations is positively associated with their satisfaction with IS use.
effects.citation_sentence: The focus of this paper is on replicating IS Continuance Model (Bhattacherjee, 2001) in the mobile banking context.
effects.evidence: Section 4.2 / Figure 2 (path 0.607): "all hypotheses are supported at p < 0.01 level ... Satisfaction was also predicted by confirmation."
effects.notes: Internal inconsistency: Figure 2 labels confirmation->satisfaction 0.607 and confirmation->PU 0.586, but the Discussion gives 0.607 as the confirmation->perceived usefulness coefficient. Either way the path is supported. See H1 notes for original_url, author name and replication type.

effects.original_title: Understanding information systems continuance: an expectation-confirmation model
effects.replication_study: single study (cross-sectional survey of mobile banking app users, SEM)
effects.contrast: not applicable: SEM path coefficient, perceived usefulness -> satisfaction
effects.description: Users' perceived usefulness of the IS is positively associated with their satisfaction with IS use.
effects.citation_sentence: The focus of this paper is on replicating IS Continuance Model (Bhattacherjee, 2001) in the mobile banking context.
effects.evidence: Section 4.2 / Figure 2 (path 0.252): "all hypotheses are supported at p < 0.01 level"; Discussion: "In both the original model and in ours, this relationship has the lowest beta weight ... (0.227 in the original research and 0.252 in our research)."
effects.notes: Supported and significant, though it is the weakest path. The Discussion argues the PU->satisfaction link is not strong and cites the later model that drops it, but it does not question the replication result. See H1 notes for original_url, author name and replication type.
